articles.full_text:
Uttarakhand chief minister
Pushkar Singh Dhami , in view of the red alert issued by the
India Meteorological Department (IMD) for the next two days, spoke to Secretary Disaster Management and Rehabilitation Vinod Kumar Suman and directed all concerned districts and departments to take necessary precautionary measures.
Dhami directed officials to maintain heightened vigilance in districts under red and orange alerts, continuously monitor vulnerable areas and ensure that all arrangements for relief and rescue operations are in place in advance in case of any emergency. He also directed that district emergency operation centres remain active and weather warnings be disseminated immediately at the local level.
Disaster management and rehabilitation minister Madan Kaushik also spoke to Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman and took stock of the weather situation and preparedness across the state. He directed officials to closely monitor the weather and remain fully prepared to deal with any eventuality.
Following the chief minister’s directions, Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman held a meeting with all 13 districts on Friday and instructed them to remain on alert mode.
According to the weather department forecast, on September 26, red alerts have been issued for five districts, orange alerts for five districts and yellow alerts for three districts.
On September 27, red alerts have been issued for four districts, orange alerts for four districts and yellow alerts for five districts.
On September 26, Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Champawat, Nainital and Udham Singh Nagar are under a red alert, while Dehradun, Pauri Garhwal, Rudraprayag, Chamoli and Almora are under an orange alert. Haridwar, Uttarkashi and Tehri Garhwal are under a yellow alert.
On September 27, red alerts have been issued for Dehradun, Tehri Garhwal, Pauri Garhwal and Haridwar; orange alerts for Uttarkashi, Chamoli, Nainital and Rudraprayag; and yellow alerts for Bageshwar, Almora, Champawat, Udham Singh Nagar and Pithoragarh.
The weather department has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall at several places and extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places. Authorities have been asked to remain particularly vigilant in view of the possibility of landslides and road blockages in hilly areas, rising water levels in rivers and streams, and waterlogging in the plains.
Suman directed all districts to continuously monitor vulnerable areas, keep district emergency operation centres operational and ensure immediate dissemination of every weather warning to the ground level.
Officials have been instructed to continuously monitor water levels in rivers, streams, gad-gaderas and other water sources and make arrangements to shift people living nearby to safer locations if water levels rise. JCBs and other necessary machinery should be stationed at strategic locations along landslide-prone roads and areas so that blocked routes can be cleared at the earliest.
All district emergency operation centres have been directed to remain operational round the clock, with continuous coordination among the police, SDRF, fire services, health, Public Works Department, drinking water, power and other concerned departments. Relief and rescue teams, along with necessary equipment and resources, should be deployed in vulnerable areas as required.
The secretary also directed that traffic on mountain routes be regulated based on weather and road conditions and unnecessary travel in areas vulnerable to landslides and heavy rainfall be avoided. People living near rivers, streams and seasonal water channels should be regularly alerted and prevented from approaching riverbanks or entering fast-flowing waters.
Special monitoring has also been ordered along the Char Dham routes, major tourist destinations and other vulnerable areas to ensure the safety of pilgrims and tourists. All arrangements should be kept ready in advance so that relief and rescue operations can begin with minimum response time in case of an emergency.

Suman urged district administrations to remain fully alert and not to show any negligence in view of the prevailing weather conditions. He also appealed to the public to follow advisories issued by the weather department and district administration, avoid unnecessary travel and stay away from rivers, streams and landslide-prone areas.
The State Emergency Operation Centre is continuously monitoring the weather situation. In case of any emergency, people can contact the State Emergency Operation Centre at toll-free number 1070, the District Emergency Operation Centre at 1077, or emergency services at 112.

articles.full_text:
New Delhi: Delhi is likely to receive light to moderate post-monsoon rainfall over the next two to three days, with India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing a yellow alert for Saturday.
The showers are expected due to a combination of weather systems despite the southwest monsoon having withdrawn from the capital earlier this week.
Weather officials said rainfall activity is likely on Saturday, Sunday and Monday, though no warning has been issued beyond Saturday.
The southwest monsoon withdrew from Delhi on Sept 23, two days ahead of its normal withdrawal date of Sept 25, marking the earliest retreat from the capital since 2002. Safdarjung, the city’s base observatory, recorded 728.6mm of rainfall during the season, about 16% above the long-period average of 629.7mm.
Meteorologists attributed the fresh spell of rain to a depression over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh, which is moving towards Uttar Pradesh, and its interaction with a weak western disturbance.
“There is a depression over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh, which is moving towards Uttar Pradesh.
There is also a feeble western disturbance, and their confluence will lead to rain. While heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Uttarakhand and northwest Uttar Pradesh, Delhi-NCR, Punjab, Haryana and north Rajasthan may receive light to moderate rainfall till Sept 28,” said Mahesh Palawat, vice-chairman of Skymet.
Moist easterly winds and cloudy skies also kept temperatures in check on Friday. The maximum temperature settled at 33°C, one degree below normal and lower than Thursday’s 35.9°C, while the minimum was 24.2°C.
IMD has forecast maximum and minimum temperatures of 32-34°C and 22-23°C, respectively, on Saturday.
Meanwhile, Delhi’s air quality improved, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) recorded at 78 in the satisfactory category.

Nepal Red Alert as Heavy Rain Triggers Landslides
Public transport services to and from Kathmandu have been suspended after floods and landslides blocked major highways across Nepal, as authorities issued red alerts for several areas ahead of widespread and intense rainfall expected through Saturday.
The Weather Forecasting Division under the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) has released a five-day special weather warning bulletin, asking people and relevant agencies to remain highly vigilant on Friday and Saturday. The bulletin warned of increasing rainfall and weather-related hazards across different parts of the country.
In Kathmandu, the Bagmati River has risen sharply and breached its embankments after more than 36 hours of continuous rain. The DHM has warned that light to heavy rainfall, along with weather-related disasters, may affect various parts of Nepal from Friday night until Tuesday.
Highway blockages caused by landslides and floods have disrupted travel between the capital and other parts of the country. Public transport operations were stopped from early Friday morning, leaving passengers stranded and making movement difficult on key routes.
Rajesh Kumar Yadav, a passenger stranded by the disruption, said vehicles could not move because the highways were blocked. He also pointed to flooding and landslides in several parts of Nepal and the rising Bagmati River in Kathmandu.
Police said public vehicles had been halted in Kathmandu after landslides obstructed traffic at multiple points along the Prithvi and BP highways. Light vehicles, however, continued to operate through the Pharping route.
Rain has persisted across the Kathmandu Valley since Thursday morning, pushing up water levels in rivers throughout the area. The Kathmandu Valley Traffic Police Office has advised residents against parking vehicles along river corridors.
Government agencies have asked residents to stay alert, with heavy rainfall forecast in different parts of Nepal between September 24 and 28.
Public vehicle operator Daniel Thakuri said operators had been following weather warnings for two days but stopped services because of the danger of landslides, blocked roads and passengers becoming stranded en route. He said operations would resume only when weather conditions became fully suitable.
The Weather Forecasting Division has asked the public and concerned agencies to take precautionary measures and remain prepared to reduce the impact of weather-related disasters.
Several hilly and Terai areas of Bagmati, Gandaki, Madhesh and Koshi provinces have been placed in the high-risk category under the red alert. Most districts in Sudurpaschim, Karnali and Lumbini provinces in western Nepal are also under alert, while parts of southern Madhesh have been included in the warning. No district was classified as green, or low risk, on Friday.
The rainfall threat is expected to intensify and expand on Saturday. Numerous hilly and mountainous districts in Sudurpaschim, Karnali, Lumbini, Gandaki and Bagmati provinces have been placed in the high-risk category for that day.
The Terai and hilly regions of western Nepal will remain under alert, although the risk is expected to decline in the eastern provinces of Koshi and Madhesh.
From Sunday, the weather system is forecast to move gradually westward, allowing conditions in eastern Nepal to improve. Most hilly and mountainous areas of Sudurpaschim, Karnali and Lumbini provinces, however, will continue to remain under alert.
The department’s warning map shows that parts of Bagmati and Madhesh provinces, along with other areas of central Nepal, will remain under regular monitoring. Districts in Koshi province are expected to move out of the warning category.
Weather conditions are expected to improve considerably across most of Nepal from Monday. Only some northwestern districts of Sudurpaschim province are likely to remain under alert, while the rest of the country is expected to leave the warning category. The forecast map for Tuesday indicates that no district is expected to remain under a weather warning.
With particularly heavy rainfall expected on Friday night and Saturday, the division has advised people living near rivers and in landslide-prone settlements to exercise extra caution.
Local administrations, security agencies and disaster management teams in red-alert areas have been directed to remain ready for emergency response and complete necessary preparedness measures.

articles.full_text:
Kerala’s entire coastline has been placed on red alert following an INCOIS warning of high waves and sudden swell surges, or Kallakkadal in Malayalam, from the early hours of Saturday, 26 September.
The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) has warned of 1 to 1.5-metre-high waves and swell surge activity from 2.30 am on 26 September to 2.30 am on 28 September.
Low-lying coastal areas are particularly vulnerable to sea surges and inundation.
Special caution has been advised along vulnerable stretches in all nine coastal districts—from Kappil to Pozhiyoor in Thiruvananthapuram and Alappad to Edava in Kollam, to Chellanam–Azheekal Jetty in Alappuzha, Munambam–Maruvakkad in Ernakulam, Aattupuram–Kodungallur in Thrissur, Kadalundi Nagaram–Palapetti in Malappuram, Chombala–Ramanattukara in Kozhikode, Valapattanam–New Mahe in Kannur and Kunchathur–Kottakkunnu in Kasaragod.
Fisherfolk and coastal residents have been urged to exercise extreme caution and follow instructions issued by the authorities.
Avoid launching or landing fishing vessels during periods of intensified wave activity.
Fishing boats and canoes should be securely moored inside harbours, with adequate spacing to prevent collisions, while fishing gear should also be secured.
Authorities have advised residents in vulnerable areas to relocate if instructed.
Beach tourism, recreational activities and trips to the sea should be completely avoided until the warning is withdrawn.
People have also been cautioned about possible coastal erosion.
Similar warnings have been issued for the coasts of Kanniyakumari, Ramanathapuram, Thoothukudi and Tirunelveli in Tamil Nadu, as well as Lakshadweep.

Red alert issued in parts of Nepal as landslide blocks highways, water level surge high following incessant rainfall
Kathmandu [Nepal], September 25 (ANI): Public transport services have been suspended, with authorities issuing a red alert for parts of Nepal as a weather system is expected to bring widespread and intense rainfall through Saturday.
The Weather Forecasting Division under the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) has issued a five-day special weather warning bulletin, urging the public and concerned agencies to remain highly alert on Friday and Saturday as rainfall and weather-related hazards are expected to increase across various parts of the country.
In the capital Kathmandu, the Bagmati River has swollen and breached its embankments following incessant rainfall for over 36 hours. The DHM, issuing the special bulletin, has further warned that light to heavy rainfall and weather-related disasters are possible in different parts of the country from Friday night through Tuesday.
Since early Friday morning, public transport services to and from Kathmandu have been suspended after several highways were obstructed by landslides and floods following incessant rainfall across the country since Thursday.
People have been facing difficulties travelling as major highways connecting Kathmandu with different parts of the country have been disrupted.
“Because of the incessant rainfall, all the vehicles have remained stranded as the highways are blocked. Passengers have also been left stranded; there are widespread floods and landslides in parts of Nepal, the Bagmati (in Kathmandu) is also swelling up. Everyone is left stranded,” Rajesh Kumar Yadav, a stranded passenger, told ANI.
The police, in a notice, said public vehicles have been halted in Kathmandu after vehicular movement was disrupted by landslides at various locations along the Prithvi and BP highways. However, light vehicles are operating via the Pharping route.
Incessant rainfall has continued in the Kathmandu Valley since Thursday morning, causing water levels in rivers across the valley to rise. The Kathmandu Valley Traffic Police Office has urged the public not to park vehicles along river corridors.
Various government agencies have urged the public to remain alert, warning that heavy rainfall could occur in different parts of the country from September 24 to 28.
“We had been receiving alerts for two days and we abided by them. Today we could not move out of Kathmandu because of the possibility of landslides and we might get stranded midway, that’s why we have halted vehicular movement during the rainfall. We are constantly following up on the weather alerts and we will only operate after the weather permits in full fledge. We have ceased our operations as the roads are also blocked, let’s see,” Daniel Thakuri, one of the public vehicle operators, told ANI.
Nepal’s Weather Forecasting Division has urged the public and concerned agencies to take necessary precautions and remain prepared to reduce the risk of weather-related disasters. Various hilly and Terai areas of Bagmati, Gandaki, Madhesh, and Koshi provinces have been placed in the high-risk category, indicated by the red alert level.
Similarly, most districts in Sudurpaschim, Karnali, and Lumbini provinces in western Nepal have been placed under alert. Some areas of southern Madhesh have also been included in the warning. No district has been placed in the green, or low-risk, category on Friday.
The risk of rainfall is expected to become more intense and widespread on Saturday. A large number of hilly and mountainous districts in Sudurpaschim, Karnali, Lumbini, Gandaki, and Bagmati provinces have been placed in the high-risk category for the day.
The Terai and hilly areas of western Nepal will remain under alert, while the risk level is expected to decrease in Koshi and Madhesh provinces in the east.
From Sunday, the weather system is expected to gradually move westward, bringing improving weather conditions to eastern Nepal. However, most hilly and mountainous areas of Sudurpaschim, Karnali, and Lumbini provinces will remain under alert.
According to the warning map issued by the Department, parts of Bagmati and Madhesh provinces and other areas of central Nepal will remain under regular monitoring, while districts in Koshi province will come out of the warning category.
From Monday, weather conditions are expected to improve significantly across most parts of the country. Only some northwestern districts of Sudurpaschim province are expected to remain under alert, while the rest of the country is likely to come out of the warning category. The warning map issued for Tuesday indicates that all districts across the country are expected to be free of weather warnings.
As rainfall is expected to be particularly intense on Friday night and Saturday, the Division has urged people living along rivers and in landslide-prone settlements to exercise special caution.
Local administrations, security agencies, and disaster management teams in areas under the high-risk red alert have been instructed to remain on standby for emergency response and take necessary preparedness measures. (ANI)

Heavy rain likely in Himachal Pradesh from Saturday, orange alert in Sirmaur
Weather department forecasts heavy to very heavy rain in parts of the state from September 26 to 29, with peak activity expected on September 27
Heavy rain is likely to lash southeastern parts of Himachal Pradesh and adjoining areas from the night of September 26 to September 29, with peak activity expected on September 27.
According to the weather department, fairly widespread rainfall, accompanied by isolated heavy rain, thunderstorms and lightning, is very likely in parts of Sirmaur, Shimla, Solan, Mandi and Bilaspur districts over the next three to four days.
The department has issued an orange alert for heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places in Sirmaur district on September 27. A yellow alert for heavy rain at isolated places has also been issued for Bilaspur, Mandi, Shimla and Solan districts for the same day.
For September 26, a yellow alert for heavy rain has been issued for Sirmaur, while isolated heavy rain is likely in Shimla and Solan districts on September 28.
The department has also warned of possible landslides and mudslides in vulnerable areas of Sirmaur district.
